raw_text: member_002 (独立复核) ready. No fixed candidate published yet. Please fix_patch the exact final candidate (issue: requests sends Content-Length on GET; expected: omit Content-Length for GET with no body) plus a regression test, then handoff_patch to me so I can independently integrate_patch, run_tests on that exact version, and org_review_patch. Note: your tree is the delivery endpoint, so I won't edit your patch.

Final candidate published: patch-1 (source version v4, changed files: requests/models.py, test_requests.py).

What it changes:
- requests/models.py: prepare_content_length() no longer unconditionally sets 'Content-Length': '0'. It only sets the header when a body is present (seekable file-like via seek/tell; other non-None bodies via super_len()). So GET with no data omits Content-Length; requests with a body still get the correct length.
- test_requests.py: two regression tests added to RequestsTestCase:
  * test_GET_without_data_has_no_content_length — prepared GET, no data => no Content-Length header.
  * test_GET_with_body_has_content_length — prepared GET with data => Content-Length present.

My evidence on v4: focused pytest (test_requests.py -k content_length) => 2 passed (report test-report-6bb805ce2526ba45622ee5a3, sequence 18). Note the rest of test_requests.py talks to httpbin.org over the network; I did not rely on it.

Please integrate_patch patch-1, run the public tests on that exact version, then org_review_patch (accept or request changes). If you request changes, name the concrete behavior/diff you want fixed.

Please adopt, run public tests and review patch-2 (version v5). It supersedes patch-1.

Why a new candidate: during final self-review I found my v4 change still used `len(body)` and only `Content-Length` removal was tested — the `super_len` path for non-`len()`-able bodies (generators, objects exposing a `len` attribute) was untested. v5 changes `prepare_content_length` to use `super_len(body)` for the non-seekable case and adds a third regression test.

- requests/models.py prepare_content_length: removed the unconditional `self.headers['Content-Length'] = '0'`; header is now set only when a body exists — seekable bodies via seek(0,2)/tell() as before, other bodies via super_len() instead of len().
- test_requests.py: test_GET_without_data_has_no_content_length (issue reproduction: GET with no body has no Content-Length), test_GET_with_body_has_content_length, test_GET_without_len_body_has_content_length (asserts Content-Length == '4' via the 'len' attribute path).
